title: Detection and Isolation of Circulating Melanoma Cells using Photoacoustic Flowmetry
protocol: Draw approximately 10 mL of whole blood from a Stage IV Cancer patient into two 5 mL vacutainers.
Centrifuge the tubes for ten minutes at 3,000 revolutions per minute (rpm).
Remove as much plasma as possible without disturbing the buffy coat.
Place 250 μL of Histopaque 1077 in two 1 mL Wintrobe tubes.
Extract the remaining plasma, the entire buffy coat, and even the top layer of erythrocytes using a 9″ Pasteur Pipette, making sure to collect less than 500 μL.
Place the extracted solution atop the Histopaque layer in the Wintrobe tubes.
Centrifuge the Wintrobe tubes in 15 mL conical tubes for 10 minutes at 3000 rpm.
Obtain the entire buffy coat using a 9″ Pasteur Pipette and place it in a 2 mL eppendorf tube.
Suspend the buffy coat in 1.5 mL of PBS with 2% v/v Tween 20.
Obtain an acrylic cylinder with specifications of 20 mm outer diameter, 17 mm inner diameter, and 8 mm height.
Drill three holes through the side of the cylinder, each with a 5 mm diameter and spaced at 90 degree angles from each other.
Cut three pieces of polymer tubing with dimensions of 1.6 mm inner diameter and 5 mm outer diameter.
Insert the cut polymer tubes into the drilled holes.
Stretch Parafilm across the bottom of the acrylic ring to create a watertight seal.
Suspend a 1.6 mm diameter wire through two opposite pieces of tubing.
Fill the third piece of tubing with another 1.6 mm diameter wire and position it 1 mm away from the suspended wire.
Allow the acrylamide solution placed in the Parafilm-sealed ring to solidify, forming a flow chamber.
Extract the wires after the acrylamide has solidified, leaving a cylindrical flow path and a place for optical fiber positioning.
Add 5 mL of prepared acrylamide solution to a small beaker.
Measure out 0.02 g of ammonium persulfate and add it to the beaker.
Mix with a stir bar for 3 minutes.
Add 20 μL tetramethylethylenediamine to the beaker.
Quickly pour the mixture into the acrylic ring, filling to the top.
Carefully pull the wires out, making sure not to disturb the acrylamide gel.
Acoustically couple a polyvinylidene fluoride piezoelectric acoustic transducer to a flow chamber using ultrasound gel directly above the flow path.
Connect the transducer to the input of a RITEC Broadband Receiver-640A using a BNC cable.
Set the lowpass filter output and highpass filter at 1 MHz for the receiver.
Configure the input impedance to 50 Ohms and amplification to 35 dB.
Connect the output of the filter to the oscilloscope (Tektronix TDS 2024B).
Plug a photodiode into the oscilloscope using a BNC cable for triggering.
Attach a t-connector to one arm of the flow chamber.
Connect two syringe pumps to the other branches of the connector.
Set one syringe pump with air and fill it as needed.
Prepare a cell suspension in another syringe pump.
Set both syringe pumps to a flow rate of 100 μL/minute.
Extract small tubing from the flow chamber until a pocket of air forms.
Insert a 1 mm diameter core optical fiber into the slot created by the extracted tubing.
Fill the pocket with water to reduce interface signals and increase laser light application.
Ensure that only one slug of sample is irradiated at any given time due to the numerical aperture of the optical fiber and distance from the flow path.
Set the laser energy to approximately 28 mJ/cm² with a spot size of 7 mm².
Turn both syringe pumps on.
Irradiate the flowing sample with a nanosecond pulsed laser to generate photoacoustic waves in the melanoma cells.
Take captured slugs to a Cytospin 4 Centrifuge.
Place glass slides into Cytofunnels.
Put 100 μL of 1% Bovine Serum Albumin in PBS into each funnel and centrifuge at 600 rpm for 3 minutes.
Add the cell samples to the Cytofunnels and then centrifuge at 600 rpm for 3 minutes.
Spray the slides with an ethanol based fixative.
Wash the slides in PBS for 10 minutes twice.
Incubate each slide with a mixture of 10 μL of Goat Serum and 90 μL of PBS for 1 hour at room temperature.
Incubate the slides with primary antibody solution for 1 hour in a humidified chamber at room temperature.
Wash the slides in PBS for 10 minutes three times.
Incubate the slides in secondary antibody solution for 1 hour in the dark at room temperature.
Wash the slides in PBS for 5 minutes three times.
Incubate the cells with DAPI for 1 minute.
Wash the slides in PBS.
Mount a coverslip over the cell sample using 20 μL of resin-based mounting media per slide.
Seal the coverslip with clear nail polish.
